findings.note: Model-id case handling is inconsistent between routing and wire rendering. route() lowercases before matching the 'codex/' prefix (internal/fsm/judge/judge.go:116-121), but wireModel strips the prefix with a case-sensitive strings.TrimPrefix, and validateCodex's empty-wire-model guard compares model == CodexPrefix exactly. A JUDGE var of 'Codex/gpt-5.6' therefore routes to the CLI arm, passes validation, and is handed to the CLI as '-m Codex/gpt-5.6' with the transport prefix still attached; the failure surfaces as an opaque 'codex exited N' (codex.go:212). The same asymmetry pre-exists for 'Anthropic/' and 'OpenAI/', so this is a consistency issue rather than a regression.

evidence.note: '-m', wireModel(r.Model) — wireModel trims case-sensitively while route() matched case-insensitively.
validateCodex guards only the exact literal 'codex/', so a differently-cased prefix bypasses the empty-wire-model check.

findings.note: The codex arm has no retry ladder: v.Attempts is hard-set to 1 and any non-zero exit or exec failure is returned immediately, while the HTTP arm retries up to MaxAttempts=5 with backoff. A transient CLI failure (a dropped OAuth refresh, a momentary spawn failure) that the HTTP providers would ride out fails the node outright. Call's doc comment promises comparable verdicts across providers but does not state this reliability asymmetry.

evidence.note: v.Attempts = 1 with no loop, versus the MaxAttempts ladder in internal/fsm/judge/judge.go:493-500.

findings.note: itoa (codex.go:284) mishandles math.MinInt: negation overflows, the digit loop never runs, and the result is a bare '-'. Dismissed as unreachable — both call sites pass a process exit status, which is 0-255 on every supported platform, and the helper is covered by internal/fsm/judge/codex_test.go:214.

evidence.note: neg := n < 0; n = -n overflows only for math.MinInt, which no exit status can be.

findings.note: Report.Outcomes is declared [2]string with explicit string() conversions, while spec 3 section 4 declares [2]run.Outcome. The JSON is byte-identical because run.Outcome is a string type, but the Go API loses the type that would keep a caller from putting an arbitrary string in an outcome slot.
